title: Attainment of Constrained Domain-Wall Energies
exact_target: Does every allowed angle and integer winding class have an energy-minimizing domain wall?

sources.citation: ULAM.AI and the UnsolvedMath Contributors, UnsolvedMath, record 30003093 (OWR-14225-001). Catalogue curation under CC BY 4.0; definitions and English exposition added locally.

Mechanics of Materials: Mechanics of Interfaces and Evolving Microstructure (2016), Oberwolfach Reports, DOI 10.4171/owr/2016/17, pp. 797--867. Primary report accessed 2026-10-11; relevant PDF pages 21, 22.
Döring--Ignat--Otto (catalogue-listed context; not independently consulted in this preparation).

status_qualification: The energy, strip and both constraints were recovered from PDF page 21. The source first singles out $q\in\{-1,0,1\}$ and also asks the general integer case, so both are retained. Its negative-end square-integrability line displays a questionable plus sign inconsistent with its stated far-field value; that sign is not silently used to define an empty class. The asymptotic notation above retains the intended boundary-state statement, and a theorem must explicitly fix its convergence convention.
